This section defines the scope and boundary of the three offshore wind
architectures evaluated by the model:

1. electricity export using AC infield collection and HVDC export
2. centralised offshore hydrogen production with one integrated offshore
   platform
3. decentralised turbine-integrated hydrogen production

The architecture pages identify which physical functions are present, where
energy conversion occurs, and how the offshore system connects to the onshore
delivery point. Component pages remain the owners of sizing methods,
assumptions, costs, losses, availability, and technical limitations.

The current Tier 1 outputs are carrier-specific. Electricity and hydrogen
results may be shown side by side, but they are not equivalent end-use service
prices.

## Comparison Boundary

The common offshore-project boundary starts with the wind turbine and its
support structure. It ends at:

- the defined onshore electrical delivery point for electricity export; or
- the defined onshore hydrogen delivery point for hydrogen export.

Infrastructure beyond those connection points is outside the model boundary.
This excludes the wider electricity network, the hydrogen backbone itself,
downstream storage, distribution, reconversion, and end use.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-height: 2.8
flowchart LR
  E1["Wind turbines"] --> E2["AC infield collection"]
  E2 --> E3["Offshore HVDC conversion"]
  E3 --> E4["HVDC export"]
  E4 --> E5["Onshore grid connection"]

  C1["Wind turbines"] --> C2["AC infield collection"]
  C2 --> C3["Central offshore electrolysis"]
  C3 --> C4["Compression and pipeline export"]
  C4 --> C5["Onshore hydrogen-backbone connection"]

  D1["Wind turbines"] --> D2["Turbine-integrated electrolysis"]
  D2 --> D3["Hydrogen infield collection"]
  D3 --> D4["Pipeline export"]
  D4 --> D5["Onshore hydrogen-backbone connection"]
```

## Architecture Distinctions

| Question | Electricity export | Centralised hydrogen | Decentralised hydrogen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carrier in the infield network | Electricity | Electricity | Hydrogen |
| Offshore conversion location | Central HVDC platform | One central electrolysis platform | At each turbine |
| Carrier exported to shore | Electricity | Hydrogen | Hydrogen |
| Central offshore platform | AC aggregation and HVDC conversion | AC aggregation and electrolysis | None |
| Onshore delivery point | Defined onshore electrical delivery point | Defined onshore hydrogen delivery point | Defined onshore hydrogen delivery point |
| Carrier-cost output | EUR~2025~/MWh-electricity | EUR~2025~/MWh-H2-HHV and EUR~2025~/kg-H2 | EUR~2025~/MWh-H2-HHV and EUR~2025~/kg-H2 |

The centralised-hydrogen architecture has one physical offshore platform. AC
aggregation, electrolyser power electronics, PEM stacks, water treatment, and
the non-electrical electrolyser balance of plant are integrated on that
platform. Compression is a separate functional and accounting subsystem, even
when it is physically hosted on the same platform.

In the decentralised-hydrogen architecture, the PEM stack connects to the
turbine DC link without a separate electrolyser-side DC/DC converter. Water
treatment belongs to the turbine-level electrolyser facility. Turbine-level
compression remains a separate downstream subsystem.

## Physical and Economic Scope

The physical energy chain contains only equipment that captures, converts,
collects, transports, or delivers energy. Installation and project-development
activities are therefore not shown as energy-flow steps.

The economic boundary nevertheless includes the lifecycle activities required
for every asset within the physical boundary:

- procurement and fabrication
- transport and installation
- commissioning
- operation, maintenance, and repair
- component replacement where represented by the model
- decommissioning where represented by the model

The shared cost schema retains required common project categories. Development,
shared engineering, insurance and owner contingency are currently unresolved;
construction finance, taxes and financing fees are excluded by the approved
simple-CRF convention. A complete result remains not parameterized while a
required shared field is unresolved.

Wider network reinforcement beyond the defined connection point is excluded.
